name: The Samaritan village, and the sons of thunder
charge: Refusing to receive him because his face was toward Jerusalem; James and John asking for fire from heaven
summary: A village of Samaria would not take him in because he was travelling toward Jerusalem, and James and John asked leave to call fire out of heaven and consume it as Elias had done (Luke 9:51-54). The village was of the northern kingdom, and the refusal was the old grudge between the two houses. He rebuked the two disciples rather than the village, told them they did not know what manner of spirit was on them, and said the Son of man came to save lives and not to destroy them, and they went on to another village (Luke 9:55-56).
offenseFull: When the time came that he should be received up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem and sent messengers ahead into a village of the Samaritans to make ready, and they would not receive him because of where he was going (Luke 9:51-53). That village was of the northern kingdom. Samaria was the head of Ephraim (Isaiah 7:9), and the Samaritans were Israelites, which is why the woman at the well appealed to their father Jacob and why the record notes that the Jews had no dealings with them (John 4:9; John 4:12). This was the beef between the two houses, not a stranger turning away a stranger. James and John, the sons of Zebedee, whom he had surnamed the sons of thunder, asked leave to command fire out of heaven and consume the village, as Elias had done to the captains sent against him (Luke 9:54; 2 Kings 1:9-12). In plain terms they wanted to burn their own brothers over a slight.

Their anger came dressed as loyalty. Just before this, John had reported that they forbade a man casting out devils in Christ’s name because he did not walk with them, and was told to forbid him not, since the man who is not against us is on our side (Luke 9:49-50). The same spirit was still running. Men teaching the same identity who do not speak against Christ are not to be hindered merely because they do not stand with us, and a brother who will not receive a labourer is not thereby marked for destruction. Rejection is real, and it falls back on the one who rejects: the man who despises the labourer despises the one who sent him, and despises not man but God (Luke 10:16; 1 Thessalonians 4:8). It was not theirs to avenge.
judgmentFull: He turned and rebuked the two, not the village, telling them they did not know what manner of spirit was on them, for the Son of man came to save men’s lives and not to destroy them, and they went to another village (Luke 9:55-56). John records the same purpose in other words, that the Son was sent to save the world and not to condemn it (John 3:17). The correction fell on the disciples who proposed the fire. The work is to win the soul, not to end it: a true witness delivers souls (Proverbs 14:25), and the man who wins souls is wise (Proverbs 11:30). The servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle toward all men, able to teach, patient, instructing in meekness those who oppose themselves, so that God may give them repentance and they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil (2 Timothy 2:24-26). Those two brothers had no patience, and that is exactly what the name they carried meant.

The rebuke prepared them. The same two had been taken up into the mountain with Peter (Luke 9:28), and they became an integral part of building up the believers and teaching them, which they could not have done carrying the temper they had on that road. John afterward went with Peter into Samaria when its people received the word of God, and prayed for them (Acts 8:14-17), serving the very people he had once asked to burn. Where a house or a city will not receive the labourer, the instruction was to shake off the dust from the feet for a testimony and go on, and the account is left with God, who will settle it in the day of judgment (Luke 9:5; Matthew 10:14-15). No fire fell on that village. The only sentence in the record is the one spoken to the men who asked for it.

text.text: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.
Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?
And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.
And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.
He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
He therefore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, who hath also given unto us his holy Spirit.
But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.
And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient,
In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;
And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.
And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
